images.title: 6 : 10 :: 18 : 30 for the lemonade
images.purpose: Shows glasses and spoons both multiplied by 3, keeping the lemonade equally sweet.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A two-row, two-column table in the centre with a factor arrow on each row.
images.exact_structure: A table of two rows and two columns with thin dark lines. Top row, headed at its left by a small teal (#0072B2) glass icon and the word glasses: cells 6 and 18. Bottom row, headed at its left by a small amber (#E69F00) spoon icon and the word spoons: cells 10 and 30. Exactly two curved reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrows, one above the top row from 6 to 18 and one below the bottom row from 10 to 30, each labelled × 3. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Same sweetness means the same factor on both terms: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so 10 × 3 = 30 spoons.
images.description: Shows glasses and spoons both multiplied by 3, keeping the lemonade equally sweet.

image_decisions.why: The table with matching arrows shows the factor of change applied to both terms.
